body.statement: For every \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\), translate its target \(Q[S_0](s_0;x_0)\) to \(Q=P((S_0)_{x_0}=s_0)\). For every \(t\ge1\) and every ordinary identifying collection \(\mathbf B=(B_1,\ldots,B_t)\), quantify the complete finite source data \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}=\{Q[V\setminus B_i](\cdot;b):i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}\) and labels \(\Lambda_{\mathbf B}=\{\ell_{i,b}:i\in[t],\ b\in\mathfrak X_{B_i}\}\). The protocols \(S_{B_i}\) are legal SELECT-RAND-READ protocols with every \(\rho_v\), their slices equal the corresponding ordinary kernels \(Q[V\setminus B_i](\cdot;b)=P_b(V\setminus B_i)\), and the explicitly constructed uniform record list \(E_{\mathbf B}\), whose ownership masks cover every \(j\in[k]\), satisfies \(\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E_{\mathbf B};G)=1\) and \(\operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathbf B})=\sum_{B\in\{B_1,\ldots,B_t\}}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v\), with the outer sum over distinct sets. Conversely, for every accepted finite \(E\) in \(\iota(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}})\), augment each protocol by missing zero-cost READ records and take the distinct RAND-endpoint sets \(\mathbf B(E)\); their full assignments generate exactly the ordinary family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B(E)}\), which identifies \(Q[S_0](\cdot;x_0)\), and \(\operatorname{Cost}(E)=\sum_{B\in\mathbf B(E)}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v\). Thus ordinary and embedded feasibility agree in both directions and their optimum costs are equal. Restricted to this image, the physical acquisition problem is exactly the 2025 JMLR ordinary intervention-design object with its fixed \(Q[S]\) source-family semantics, so its ordinary complexity and approximation guarantees transfer only on that image; outside the image, CTF-RAND actions, partial child effects, reusable slices, precedence, conflicts, and the charged source-support interface are additional objects. In the 2025 JMLR article, Theorem 1 on page 5 supplies the singleton reduction for a c-component target, Lemma 3 on page 8 supplies the minimum-weight hedge-hitting equivalence, Theorems 2 and 3 on pages 6--7 give polynomial reductions from weighted vertex cover and minimum-weight hitting set, Corollaries 1 and 2 on pages 7--8 give NP-completeness and logarithmic inapproximability, Lemma 7 on page 12 certifies exact Algorithm 2, and Proposition 3 on page 16 certifies the general-target exact Algorithm 3.
body.justification: The two-way embedding matches the ordinary \(Q[S]\) target and source-family semantics before certifying legality, acceptance, and exact cost preservation.
body.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025), Theorem 1 on page 5, Lemma 3 on page 8, Lemma 7 on page 12, and Proposition 3 on page 16 concern ordinary intervention collections and their fixed \(Q[S]\) source families. They do not prove the two-way Layer-2.5 translation with explicit oracle-returned support, finite assignment labels, adequate READ records, complete-run acceptance, and exact protocol-cost preservation established here.
body.consumer: The equivalence transfers the ordinary hardness frontier without silently enlarging the source family or changing the causal query.

obligation.what_is_open: The unresolved part is accepted uniform-certificate construction and the reverse feasibility equivalence, not the Layer-2.5 slice translation or cost accounting.
obligation.obstruction: The definition of \(E_{\mathbf B}\) assigns one fixed labelled source and transcript to each factor by invoking the unresolved uniform-source theorem. Ordinary source-family identification provides all assignment slices of a purchased intervention set, but it does not by itself prove that one of those concrete slices is uniform over \(\Omega_j\).
obligation.attempted: I checked legality, positive assignment support, exact slice equality, zero-cost READ augmentation, recovery of the ordinary RAND-endpoint family, and distinct-protocol cost preservation in both directions. The proof stops exactly at uniform ownership and does not substitute a smaller ordinary class.
obligation.partial_result:
For a distinct ordinary intervention set \(B\), the embedded mask \(S_B\) contains one fresh SELECT, one RAND action for each \(v\in B\), and every zero-cost READ.  The construction makes it precedence closed, conflict free, mechanism-once, and physically compatible.  Independence and uniformity of its RAND labels give positive probability to every \(b\in\mathfrak X_B\), and consistency of the translated regime gives
\[
 \operatorname{Slice}(S_B,\ell_{B,b})
   =P_b(V\setminus B)=Q[V\setminus B](\,\cdot\,;b).
\]
Distinct protocols are indexed by distinct \(B\), so their cost is
\[
 \sum_{B\text{ distinct}}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v.
\]
Conversely, every protocol in the image has a unique RAND-endpoint set \(B\); adding missing READ actions changes neither legality nor cost, and all its positive RAND-label slices recover the full ordinary source family for that \(B\).  Thus protocol legality, slice semantics, and cost preservation hold in both directions.  The unresolved point is the construction of the accepted record list \(E_{\mathbf B}\): its definition invokes the unproved assertion that one fixed labelled slice and transcript can own each factor uniformly over \(\Omega_j\).  Without that quantifier step, the claimed equality between ordinary feasibility and the present uniform-certificate acceptance predicate has not been proved.
